title: Prof Paul Gilbert OBE: Lessons on Compassion, Failure & Success in Psychology

sentences.en: Psychologists, what if you could earn money beyond trading your time for money?
sentences.zh: 心理学家们，如果你们能通过出卖时间赚钱之外还能赚到钱，会怎么样？

sentences.en: I'm Dr Marianne Trent, clinical psychologist, and I've been developing passive and recurring income streams since 2019.
sentences.zh: 我是临床心理学家玛丽安·特伦特博士，自2019年以来，我一直在开发被动收入和循环收入流。

sentences.en: I have some exciting news.
sentences.zh: 我有一个好消息。

sentences.en: Sophie Foote's One-to-Many programme is now open for enrolment.
sentences.zh: 苏菲·富特的“一对多”项目现在开放报名了。

sentences.en: It's designed to help you turn your expertise into scalable offers like courses, memberships and digital products.
sentences.zh: 它旨在帮助你将专业知识转化为可扩展的产品，例如课程、会员资格和数字产品。

sentences.en: I completed the programme myself in 2022 and have since supported two cohorts of psychologists through their journeys too.
sentences.zh: 我自己在2022年完成了这个项目，此后也支持了两届心理学家走过他们的历程。

sentences.en: And if you join through my affiliate link, you'll receive Sophie's bonuses plus my own exclusive support package at no extra coSt.
sentences.zh: 如果你通过我的联盟链接加入，你将获得苏菲的奖金以及我独家提供的支持套餐，无需额外费用。

sentences.en: That includes six months of WhatsApp support, four group masterminds, masterclasses, personalised guidance, a Fortnum and Mason treat, and a time-limited one-to-one coaching bonus.
sentences.zh: 其中包括六个月的WhatsApp支持、四个小组智囊团、大师班、个性化指导、福特纳姆与梅森的精美礼品以及限时的一对一教练指导福利。

sentences.en: Enrolment closes on Monday the 16th of November at 10pm.
sentences.zh: 报名截止时间为11月16日星期一晚上10点。

sentences.en: Find out more via my bonus page linked in the description.
sentences.zh: 通过简介中链接的我的福利页面了解更多信息。

sentences.en: And remember, you must purchase through my link to receive my bonuses.
sentences.zh: 请记住，你必须通过我的链接购买才能获得我的福利。

sentences.en: I'm here if you have any questions.
sentences.zh: 如果你有任何问题，我随时都在。

sentences.en: My name's Yana, and I'm a trainee psychological wellbeing practitioner.
sentences.zh: 我叫亚娜，是一名见习心理健康从业者。

sentences.en: I read the Clinical Psychologist Collective book.
sentences.zh: 我读了《临床心理学家合集》这本书。

sentences.en: I found it really interesting about all the different stories and how people got to become a clinical psychologiSt.
sentences.zh: 我发现所有这些不同的故事以及人们如何成为临床心理学家的经历真的很有趣。

sentences.en: It just amazed me how many different routes there are to get there, and there's no perfect way to become one.
sentences.zh: 达到这个目标竟然有这么多不同的途径，这让我感到十分惊奇，而且成为临床心理学家并没有一条完美的必经之路。

sentences.en: And this kind of filled me with confidence that, no, I'm not doing it wrong, and put less pressure on myself.
sentences.zh: 这让我充满了信心，觉得自己并没有做错，同时也减轻了我的压力。

sentences.en: So if you're feeling a bit uneasy about becoming a clinical psychologist, I'd definitely recommend this, just to put yourself at ease, and everything will be okay.
sentences.zh: 所以，如果你对成为一名临床心理学家感到有些不安，我绝对推荐你读这本书，它能让你安心，一切都会好起来的。

sentences.en: But trust me, you will not put the book down once you start.
sentences.zh: 相信我，一旦你开始读，就绝对放不下这本书。

sentences.en: Professor Paul Gilbert, OBE, is one of the most influential psychologists of our time.
sentences.zh: 保罗·吉尔伯特教授，OBE，是我们这个时代最具影响力的心理学家之一。

sentences.en: And today, I have the absolute privilege of speaking with him.
sentences.zh: 今天，我有幸与他进行交流。

sentences.en: In this episode, he shares lessons from a lifetime of work on compassion, shame, failure, and success.
sentences.zh: 在本期节目中，他分享了他一生致力于同情、羞耻、失败和成功研究所获得的经验教训。

sentences.en: And what they mean for us right now as psychologists, and for the next generation of psychologists too.
sentences.zh: 以及这些经验对于我们现今的心理学家以及下一代心理学家意味着什么。

sentences.en: I'm Dr. Marianne, a qualified clinical psychologiSt.
sentences.zh: 我是玛丽安博士，一名合格的临床心理学家。

sentences.en: And if you like this content, subscribe, comment, share, do all those good things.
sentences.zh: 如果你喜欢这个内容，请订阅、评论、分享，做好所有这些好事情。

sentences.en: And I hope you love it as much as I do.
sentences.zh: 希望你和我都一样喜欢它。

sentences.en: Hi, welcome along to the Aspiring Psychologist podcaSt.
sentences.zh: 嗨，欢迎收听《有志心理学家播客》。

sentences.en: I am thrilled to be joined today by our guest, Professor Paul Gilbert, OBE.
sentences.zh: 今天非常高兴能邀请到我们的嘉宾保罗·吉尔伯特教授，OBE。

sentences.en: Welcome, Paul.
sentences.zh: 欢迎你，保罗。

sentences.en: Well, thank you so much, Marianne, for inviting me.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你，玛丽安，邀请我来。

sentences.en: Well, thank you for saying yes, because I know you're a very busy man.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你答应邀请，因为我知道你是个大忙人。

sentences.en: And I thought, firstly, today, I'd really love to talk to you about the psychology career.
sentences.zh: 首先，今天我真的很想和你聊聊心理学职业生涯。

sentences.en: And during this episode, celebrating 200 episodes of the Aspiring Psychologist podcast, I'd really love to, I guess, firstly, thank you.
sentences.zh: 在庆祝《有志心理学家播客》播出200期的这一期节目中，我真的很想，我想首先对你说声谢谢。

sentences.en: Because I discovered your book, The Compassionate Mind, the big yellowy orange one, in 2018 after my dad had died.
sentences.zh: 因为2018年我父亲去世后，我发现了你的书《同情心心灵》，也就是那本大大的黄橙色的书。

sentences.en: But I had this sliding doors moment where I could have discovered it sooner.
sentences.zh: 但我经历了一个滑门时刻，我本可以更早发现它。

sentences.en: So at that stage, I was in my doctorate for clinical psychology.
sentences.zh: 当时我正在攻读临床心理学博士学位。

sentences.en: And there was a number of books on a sideboard, a kind of a gathering we'd had.
sentences.zh: 我们在一次聚会上，侧柜上摆着好几本书。

sentences.en: And one of my cohort had said, does anyone want to borrow any of these books?
sentences.zh: 我的一位同窗曾问过，有人想借这些书吗？

sentences.en: And I know that's an author's worst nightmare, that these books are all being shared around and we get no royalties.
sentences.zh: 我知道这是作者的噩梦，这些书都被传阅了，而我们拿不到版税。

sentences.en: But and I looked at it and I saw the size of it, I have to say, Paul.
sentences.zh: 但是，保罗，当我看着它时，我不得不说，我看到了它的厚度。

sentences.en: And I was like, no, no, thanks.
sentences.zh: 当时我想，不，不用了，谢谢。

sentences.en: But actually, when I then had the time to listen to it in 2018, when I think I needed it most, I was like, what if I had to pick that up in 2010?
sentences.zh: 但实际上，当我后来在2018年有时间去听它时，正是我最需要它的时候，我想：要是我在2010年就拿起这本书会怎样？

sentences.en: How might that have helped me to go through training more compassionately to, you know,
sentences.zh: 那会如何帮助我更有同理心地完成培训，你知道的，

sentences.en: be pregnant and to birth my children and kind of have them when they were younger and support me in my relationships and in grief and all of that stuff.
sentences.zh: 怀孕、生孩子，在他们年幼时陪伴他们，在我的关系和悲伤中支持我以及所有这些事情。

sentences.en: And I just wanted to say thank you for what you do for me, but also, you know, the world, really, and the psychology community, because it it really matters.
sentences.zh: 我只是想对你所做的一切表示感谢，不仅为了我，也为了世界，为了心理学界，因为这真的很重要。

sentences.en: So thank you.
sentences.zh: 所以，谢谢你。

sentences.en: How wonderful is that?
sentences.zh: 这真是太棒了，不是吗？

sentences.en: OK, I think I'll stop at this point.
sentences.zh: 好吧，我想我就到这里停一下。

sentences.en: That's just wonderful.
sentences.zh: 这真是太棒了。

sentences.en: Yeah, but like, even this podcast has been so informed by you and your work, you know, I thought, well, if we could have a compassionate voice guiding people through their career,
sentences.zh: 是的，甚至这个播客也深受你和你的工作的影响，你知道的，我想，如果我们能有一个充满同情心的声音来引导人们的职业生涯，

sentences.en: and I was in the position when I was 22, 23, I would say I was working in Milton Keynes Council, doing some work with physically disabled adults.
sentences.zh: 当我22、23岁的时候，我在米尔顿凯恩斯市议会工作，做一些针对身体残疾成年人的工作。

sentences.en: I didn't know any clinical psychologists at the time, and obviously the internet was around, but it was very different and podcasts weren't really a thing at all, I think,
sentences.zh: 那时我不认识任何临床心理学家，当然互联网当时已经存在，但非常不同，播客在那个阶段，我想，

sentences.en: at that stage.
sentences.zh: 根本算不上什么流行事物。

sentences.en: And I thought, what if people have the competences and the capabilities to develop into a really great, you know, HCPC psych one day, but they don't currently,
sentences.zh: 我在想，如果人们有能力、有才能在某天成长为一个非常优秀的、你知道的HCPC心理学家，但他们目前却无法做到，

sentences.en: they can't currently get in the room to be having those conversations or to be able to expand their knowledge or to tune into, you know, the mighty
sentences.zh: 他们目前无法进入那个房间进行那些对话，或者无法扩展他们的知识，或者无法收听，你知道的，伟大的

sentences.en: Paul Gilbert.
sentences.zh: 保罗·吉尔伯特。

sentences.en: So that's why the podcast was born, to be able to kind of level the playing field a little bit, but also to up the compassion in this, in this career.
sentences.zh: 这就是播客诞生的原因，为了在某种程度上拉平竞争环境，同时也为了在这个职业中提升同情心。

sentences.en: Well, that's wonderful.
sentences.zh: 这太棒了。

sentences.en: And congratulations on 200 episodes.
sentences.zh: 祝贺你迎来第200期节目。

sentences.en: That's amazing.
sentences.zh: 太惊人了。

sentences.en: That's an amazing amount of work and effort.
sentences.zh: 这是一项惊人的工作和努力。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: Yeah, it is.
sentences.zh: 是的，确实如此。

sentences.en: And it's, it's 200 weeks.
sentences.zh: 而且已经200周了。

sentences.en: So it's a, it's been a weekly podcast, because I fear that if I ever, if I ever had a week off,
sentences.zh: 所以它是一档周播播客，因为我担心如果我哪怕休息一周，

sentences.en: I wouldn't want to go back because I'd realise how nice it is to have a little bit more time.
sentences.zh: 我就不想再继续做了，因为我会意识到拥有更多一点的时间是多么美好。

sentences.en: But I'm passionate about it.
sentences.zh: 但我对此充满热情。

sentences.en: And I'm passionate about the, the people who listen to it and to value it.
sentences.zh: 我对听这档节目的人以及重视它的人充满热情。

sentences.en: So let's, let's think a little bit about, about you and your career, Paul.
sentences.zh: 那么，让我们来聊聊你和你的职业生涯，保罗。

sentences.en: Tell us about, tell us about you and what kind of brought you to where we are now.
sentences.zh: 给我们讲讲你以及是什么引领你走到今天的。

sentences.en: Well, it's a slightly interesting career because originally I always wanted to be a psychologist in the 60s, but in those days they said, oh no,
sentences.zh: 这是一个略显有趣的职业生涯，因为最初在60年代我总是想成为一名心理学家，但在那个年代他们说，哦，不，

sentences.en: psychology is not much of a career for you.
sentences.zh: 心理学对你来说算不上什么好职业。

sentences.en: And I was studying economics.
sentences.zh: 当时我正在学经济学。

sentences.en: They said, no, that'll be much better for you.
sentences.zh: 他们说，不，那个对你更好。

sentences.en: So I did do that.
sentences.zh: 所以我确实照做了。

sentences.en: I got a degree in economics, but while I was going through, I was also reading psychology books and think, no, I want to do that.
sentences.zh: 我获得了经济学学位，但在学习的过程中，我也在读心理学书籍，心想，不，我想做那个。

sentences.en: And in those days you could do changeover courses.
sentences.zh: 在那个年代，你可以参加转专业课程。

sentences.en: And so I did a changeover course.
sentences.zh: 所以我参加了一个转专业课程。

sentences.en: And what that meant is that they would take people with other degrees and then you could do an MSc in psychology, experimental psychology, fast track it.
sentences.zh: 这意味着他们会招收拥有其他学位的人，然后你可以攻读心理学硕士学位，实验心理学，走捷径。

sentences.en: So it was a very intense course.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一个非常紧凑的课程。

sentences.en: So I went down to Sussex in 73, 74 and did the MSc down there.
sentences.zh: 因此我在73、74年去了萨塞克斯，并在那里攻读了硕士学位。

sentences.en: Now it turned out I wasn't very good at neurophysiology.
sentences.zh: 结果证明我并不擅长神经生理学。

sentences.en: So I failed my neurophysiology and had to stay there for another year.
sentences.zh: 所以我神经生理学不及格，不得不呆在那里多读一年。

sentences.en: So I needed some money.
sentences.zh: 所以我需要钱。

sentences.en: So I went and worked as a night nurse in the psychiatric and acute unit in Brighton.
sentences.zh: 于是我去布赖顿的精神病学和急性病房当了一名夜班护士。

sentences.en: And that was interesting because in those days we used to have all the young people coming down from London and taking loads of drugs on Brighton Beach and then ending up as our guests because they'd sort of lost it a bit.
sentences.zh: 这很有趣，因为在那个年代，所有年轻人都会从伦敦来到布赖顿海滩服用大量毒品，然后最终成了我们的“客人”，因为他们有点精神失常了。

sentences.en: So it was very interesting.
sentences.zh: 所以这非常有趣。

sentences.en: I learned an awful lot during that year on acute psychiatry.
sentences.zh: 在那一年急性精神病学的经历中，我学到了极其丰富的东西。

sentences.en: I always wanted to be a clinician.
sentences.zh: 我一直想成为一名临床医生。

sentences.en: So I studied very hard neurophysiology and managed to pass, obviously.
sentences.zh: 所以我非常努力地学习神经生理学，显然最终通过了考试。

sentences.en: And then set off and I started off in Birmingham, but we then went to Edinburgh.
sentences.zh: 然后我出发了，我最初在伯明翰开始工作，但后来我们去了爱丁堡。

sentences.en: I went to an Edinburgh MRC unit and that was good for me because I was on an acute ward.
sentences.zh: 我去了爱丁堡医学研究理事会（MRC）单位，这对我很合适，因为我在一个急性病房工作。

sentences.en: Again, we used to take people from all over Scotland with chronic depression.
sentences.zh: 同样，我们过去常常接收来自苏格兰各地患有慢性抑郁症的人。

sentences.en: And so I had a little office on the ward and the Prof Ashcroft, who was the professor of psychiatry, lovely man, long passed away now, said, look,
sentences.zh: 所以我在病房里有一个小办公室，精神病学教授阿什克罗夫特教授——一位可爱的人，现在已经去世很久了——对我说，听着，

sentences.en: the best way to understand depression is to go and talk to depressed people.
sentences.zh: 理解抑郁症的最好方法就是去和抑郁症患者交谈。

sentences.en: And you've got lots of them here.
sentences.zh: 这里有很多人。

sentences.en: So I used to do that, I used to go into the ward and go around and chat to people and learn a lot about stories.
sentences.zh: 所以我过去常常这样做，我会在病房里四处走动，跟人们聊天，了解了很多他们的故事。

sentences.en: And part of the themes that came out of that was obviously the history of abuse.
sentences.zh: 从中得出的主题之一显然是虐待史。

sentences.en: That was one thing.
sentences.zh: 那是其中一件事。

sentences.en: Genetic vulnerability was another thing.
sentences.zh: 基因易感性是另一件事。

sentences.en: And also the sense of defeat and entrapment and lostness that shunned through those people's experience.
sentences.zh: 还有那些在这些人的经历中闪现的失败感、受困感和迷失感。

sentences.en: And for those of you who know my research, that became a big issue of looking at issues of feelings of social defeat and entrapment and so on.
sentences.zh: 对于熟悉我研究的人来说，这成为了一个重要课题，即研究社会失败感和受困感等问题。

sentences.en: And there's been a big series of studies on that now.
sentences.zh: 现在已经有很多关于这方面的系列研究了。

sentences.en: So they got the PhD and,
sentences.zh: 于是我获得了博士学位，

sentences.en: oh, by the way, while I was in Brighton, the one year I met my beloved because I used to play cricket for the university and she used to keep the score.
sentences.zh: 哦，顺便说一句，我在布赖顿的那一年遇到了我的挚爱，因为我曾为大学板球队打球，而她负责记分。

sentences.en: So that was nice, wasn't it, really?
sentences.zh: 所以这挺美好的，不是吗？

sentences.en: And we've been together ever since.
sentences.zh: 从那以后我们一直在一起。

sentences.en: So we toddled off to Edinburgh and the thing about Edinburgh was because it was an MRC unit, they were all doing these studies on drugs and everything.
sentences.zh: 于是我们动身去了爱丁堡，爱丁堡的特点是，由于它是一个医学研究理事会单位，大家都在做这些药物及其他方面的研究。

sentences.en: If you didn't understand neurophysiology, you didn't have any friends at lunchtime.
sentences.zh: 如果你不懂神经生理学，午餐时间你就没有朋友。

sentences.en: So I'd have all these psychiatrists saying, oh, you know, depression is all to do with these receptors in the brain.
sentences.zh: 所以我会遇到所有这些精神病学家说，哦，你知道的，抑郁症全都是关于大脑中的这些受体的。

sentences.en: And I said, yes, that's important.
sentences.zh: 我说，是的，这很重要。

sentences.en: But could they all be created by psychological and social processes?
sentences.zh: 但它们会不会全都是由心理和社会过程产生的呢？

sentences.en: So my first book was called Depression from Psychology to Brain State in 1984.
sentences.zh: 所以我的第一本书名为《抑郁症：从心理学到脑状态》，出版于1984年。

sentences.en: And that was really arguing the ways in which psychological and social processes can have major impacts on the brain.
sentences.zh: 该书真正探讨的是心理和社会过程如何对大脑产生重大影响。

sentences.en: And in 1975, Martin Selwyn came out with his book, Learned Helplessness, showing these massive changes in physiology when people are confronted with uncontrollable stresses.
sentences.zh: 1975年，马丁·塞利格曼出版了他的书《习得性无助》，展示了当人们面对无法控制的压力时，生理学方面发生的这些巨大变化。

sentences.en: And that's really quite important because, as you know, we have a biopsychosocial approach that when you're working with depressed patients, they feel really ill.
sentences.zh: 这实际上非常重要，因为如你所知，我们有一种生物心理社会方法：当你与抑郁症患者一起工作时，他们会觉得自己病得很重。

sentences.en: I mean, physiologically, they're not well.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，从生理学上讲，他们很不舒服。

sentences.en: Then that doesn't mean to say they have an endogenous illness, but they are really not well.
sentences.zh: 但这并不意味着他们患有内源性疾病，但他们的确很不舒服。

sentences.en: And the sleep cycle is off, the circadian rhythm is off.
sentences.zh: 睡眠周期失调了，昼夜节律失调了。

sentences.en: Dopamine systems have pretty much collapsed for some of the severe depressions.
sentences.zh: 对于某些严重抑郁症患者来说，多巴胺系统几乎已经崩溃。

sentences.en: It was always important to keep in mind that you're not just dealing with negative schemas or beliefs or whatever,
sentences.zh: 始终要记住的一点是，你不仅在处理消极图式、信念或其他什么，

sentences.en: but actually dealing with somebody whose brain and body have kind of been affected by the depression.
sentences.zh: 实际上你面对的是一个其大脑和身体已经受到抑郁症影响的人。

sentences.en: And therefore, you're going to need a therapy that's going to have some kind of physiological effect.
sentences.zh: 因此，你需要一种能够产生某种生理效用的疗法。

sentences.en: So that was always sort of in my mind, really.
sentences.zh: 所以这实际上一直铭刻在我的脑海里。

sentences.en: So that was, then I decided I wanted to be a researcher.
sentences.zh: 然后，我决定成为一名研究人员。

sentences.en: I was going to go to Stanford.
sentences.zh: 我本打算去斯坦福大学。

sentences.en: And my beloved and I got married on the basis of that because we were living together.
sentences.zh: 以此为基础，我和我的挚爱结婚了，因为我们当时正同居。

sentences.en: And that was fine.
sentences.zh: 这挺好的。

sentences.en: And then they said, in Edinburgh, they said, oh, no, stay and do the clinical training.
sentences.zh: 然后他们在爱丁堡说，哦，不，留下来完成临床培训吧。

sentences.en: I said, no, no, I go to Stanford, you know, you know.
sentences.zh: 我说，不，不，我要去斯坦福，你知道的。

sentences.en: But when I was just about to go, I had a letter to say there'd been a complication with the department.
sentences.zh: 但就在我即将出发的时候，我收到了一封信，说部门出现了一些状况。

sentences.en: The department was on some kind of investigation.
sentences.zh: 该部门正在接受某种调查。

sentences.en: So they couldn't honour the job.
sentences.zh: 所以他们无法兑现这份工作。

sentences.en: Nowadays, of course, I'd sue them.
sentences.zh: 当然，现在我会起诉他们。

sentences.en: But in those days, I just sort of wandered off with my leg, a tail between my legs.
sentences.zh: 但在那个年代，我只是灰溜溜地夹着尾巴走开了。

sentences.en: But luckily, I managed to get a place on a clinical course in Norwich.
sentences.zh: 但幸运的是，我设法在诺维奇的一个临床课程中获得了一个名额。

sentences.en: So in 1978, we headed down to Norwich and I became, started to train as a clinical psychologist with what was then the BPS diploma.
sentences.zh: 因此，在1978年，我们前往诺维奇，我开始通过当时的英国心理学会（BPS）文凭接受临床心理学家培训。

sentences.en: And so that's how I got into clinical psychology by various routes.
sentences.zh: 这就是我通过各种途径进入临床心理学的方式。

sentences.en: And the interesting thing about economics was economics was always about building models.
sentences.zh: 关于经济学，有趣的是，经济学一直都是关于构建模型的。

sentences.en: So you had to, in the first year, you'd understand some unemployment and the terms of trade and how the money supply works.
sentences.zh: 所以在第一年，你得了解一些失业问题、贸易条件以及货币供给是如何运作的。

sentences.en: And then you'd second year, you'd start to see how economies work and so on.
sentences.zh: 然后在第二年，你开始了解经济是如何运作的，诸如此类。

sentences.en: When I got to psychology, it was odd because you'd have a course on motivation, a course on child development.
sentences.zh: 当我进入心理学时，这很奇怪，因为你会有一门关于动机的课程，一门关于儿童发展的课程。

sentences.en: There was no integrated thinking at all.
sentences.zh: 根本没有任何综合性的思考。

sentences.en: And when I said to people that were talking to me, training me, I said, well, what about an integrated model of the mind?
sentences.zh: 当我向那些与我交谈、对我进行培训的人提出时，我说，那么关于心理的综合模型呢？

sentences.en: How does these things all work together?
sentences.zh: 这些事情是如何协同工作的？

sentences.en: And they kind of looked into their beer and said, oh, no, that's too complicated.
sentences.zh: 他们端起啤酒陷入沉思，然后说，哦，不，那太复杂了。

sentences.en: No, we don't do that.
sentences.zh: 不，我们不那样做。

sentences.en: We just study these different bits.
sentences.zh: 我们只研究这些不同的部分。

sentences.en: We're very scientific.
sentences.zh: 我们非常科学。

sentences.en: We're going to study language.
sentences.zh: 我们要研究语言。

sentences.en: We study language.
sentences.zh: 我们研究语言。

sentences.en: We don't think about how language affects motivation.
sentences.zh: 我们不怎么考虑语言如何影响动机。

sentences.en: So I thought, well, in order for us to have models about how and why people become mentally and mental health difficulties or what we can do,
sentences.zh: 所以我想，为了让我们建立起关于人们如何以及为什么会陷入心理和精神健康困境的模型，或者我们能做些什么，

sentences.en: we need to understand how the mind works as a system, right?
sentences.zh: 我们需要理解心灵是如何作为一个系统运作的，对吧？

sentences.en: So you need to understand.
sentences.zh: 所以你需要去理解。

sentences.en: So when you look at compassion-focused therapy, which we'll talk about a little bit later, you'll find that really it's rooted in all the basic psychological sciences.
sentences.zh: 因此，当你了解聚焦于同情心的疗法时——我们稍后会详细讨论——你会发现它其实根植于所有基础心理科学之中。

sentences.en: And that's why I think psychologists in particular like them, because we don't root it in cognitive systems or motivational systeMs.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么我认为心理学家尤其喜欢它们，因为我们并非将其根植于认知系统或动机系统。

sentences.en: You need to think about all of those.
sentences.zh: 你需要考虑所有这些方面。

sentences.en: So if you look at the standard psychology textbook, which you would have done in your undergraduate days, there is a whole literature on motives and how motives work.
sentences.zh: 因此，如果你翻看标准的心理学教材，也就是你在本科阶段读过的那些，就会发现有一整套关于动机及其运作机制的文献。

sentences.en: There's a whole literature on emotions.
sentences.zh: 有一整套关于情绪的文献。

sentences.en: And there's a whole literature on cognitive processes, problem-solving, mindfulness, and so on.
sentences.zh: 还有一整套关于认知过程、问题解决、正念等等的文献。

sentences.en: The problem is when people turn up, clinical psychologists turn up for training, they've kind of forgotten all that.
sentences.zh: 问题在于，当人们走进门、临床心理学家开始接受培训时，他们差不多把这些全忘光了。

sentences.en: And so they're just trying to work in a model, you know, a CBT model or a DBT model or the AGB model, whatever it is.
sentences.zh: 于是他们只是试图在某个模型中工作，你知道的，比如CBT模型、DBT模型或ACT模型，诸如此类。

sentences.en: They're trying to fit all these complicated processes into a single model, and they simply won't fit.
sentences.zh: 他们试图把所有这些复杂的进程塞进一个单一的模型里，而这根本装不下。

sentences.en: And that's why we are not as forward, I believe, in our psychological therapies as we could be.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么我认为我们的心理疗法并没有像本可以做到的那样取得长足进步。

sentences.en: Now, a lot of the models are getting much more biopsychosocial.
sentences.zh: 现在，很多模型正变得越来越偏向生物心理社会模式。

sentences.en: They're beginning to understand that you need interventions that are going to have physiological effects and social effects and so on and so on.
sentences.zh: 他们开始明白，你需要那些能够产生生理效应、社会效应等等的干预措施。

sentences.en: But I think if you're an aspiring psychologist, bring your psychological science to what you're doing.
sentences.zh: 但我想，如果你是一个有志于此的心理学家，请将你的心理学科学带入你所做的事情中。

sentences.en: Don't get trapped up in one of these schools of therapy.
sentences.zh: 不要被困在其中某一个疗法流派里。

sentences.en: They're very useful and they have a lot of things to say about interventions and so on.
sentences.zh: 它们非常有用，并且对干预措施等有很多独到的见解。

sentences.en: But always stay a psychologist, right?
sentences.zh: 但永远要保持心理学家的思维，对吧？

sentences.en: Don't label yourself or think of yourself as a CBT therapist or a psychodynamic therapist or emotion-focused therapy or a body-based therapiSt.
sentences.zh: 不要给自己贴标签，也别把自己当作纯粹的CBT治疗师、心理动力学治疗师、焦点情绪治疗师或身体导向治疗师。

sentences.en: All of those approaches have fantastic wisdoms for intervention.
sentences.zh: 所有这些方法都包含极为丰富的干预智慧。

sentences.en: But when it comes to thinking about what are we dealing with here, how are bodies and minds working, then you are the best position.
sentences.zh: 但当我们需要思考我们面对的是什么、身体和心灵是如何运作的时，你才处于最佳的位置。

sentences.en: You are the best profession because you're the one that has studied the mind.
sentences.zh: 你是最好的职业，因为你是那个研究过心灵的人。

sentences.en: You're the one that's studying motivations and emotions and so on.
sentences.zh: 你是那个研究动机、情绪等等的人。

sentences.en: And so you can bring your own wisdoms into what you're doing.
sentences.zh: 因此，你可以把自己的智慧融入你所做的工作中。

sentences.en: So we're very keen on that, that psychologists don't sort of get caught up in just being this type of therapist or that type of therapiSt.
sentences.zh: 所以我们非常坚持这一点，即心理学家不应该陷入仅仅成为这种治疗师或那种治疗师的泥潭。

sentences.en: Be a psychologist that learns how to use those interventions, but put it within a conceptually scientific model of the mind.
sentences.zh: 要做一个懂得如何使用这些干预手段的心理学家，但要将它们置于一个概念化的科学心灵模型之中。

sentences.en: Amazing.
sentences.zh: 太棒了。

sentences.en: That's so interesting and so helpful.
sentences.zh: 这真的太有趣、太有帮助了。

sentences.en: Could you give us almost like a practical example of what that might look like?
sentences.zh: 你能给我们举个具体的例子，看看这可能会是什么样吗？

sentences.en: If someone finds themselves in a ward round and they're thinking,
sentences.zh: 如果有人发现自己正在查房，而他们心里想的是：

sentences.en: I don't feel like there's a very psychological conversation happening about this person or this kind of set of circumstances that we're talking about.
sentences.zh: 我觉得我们对这个人、或者我们正在讨论的这一套情况，并没有展开非常具有心理学视角的对话。

sentences.en: How could someone use their psychological underpinnings and insights to just have a different conversation in that room, Paul?
sentences.zh: 保罗，一个人该如何运用他们的心理学基础和洞察力，在那个房间里开启一段完全不同的对话呢？

sentences.en: Yeah, well, it depends.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这个得看情况。

sentences.en: You see, for example, if you're working with somebody who's hearing voice, if you're in an acute unit, you're hearing with somebody's hearing voices.
sentences.zh: 你看，举个例子，如果你在和听到幻听的人工作，如果你身处一个急性病房，你在和一个能听到声音的人在一起。

sentences.en: You say, well, from a psychological point of view, we need to understand, is there trauma in this person's background?
sentences.zh: 你会说，从心理学的角度来看，我们需要了解，这个人的背景中是否存在创伤？

sentences.en: We need to understand are there certain triggers of these voices, you know, and if we listen to these voices, are they telling us something about motivations or underlying fears?
sentences.zh: 我们需要了解这些幻听是否有某些触发因素，你知道的，如果我们倾听这些声音，它们是否在向我们传达某些关于动机或潜在恐惧的信息？

sentences.en: So, the great thing about a psychologist is you think psychologically.
sentences.zh: 所以，心理学家的伟大之处在于你习惯进行心理学思考。

sentences.en: I mean, it may sound obvious, but actually it isn't.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这听起来可能显而易见，但实际上并非如此。

sentences.en: And when you're in a ward round where other people are thinking about medications or symptom profiles or the regulation of symptoms,
sentences.zh: 当你在查房时，其他人都在考虑药物、症状特征或症状的控制，

sentences.en: you're thinking of the person living with a mind in their context and their history.
sentences.zh: 而你考虑的是一个带着心灵生活在特定语境和历史中的人。

sentences.en: All of that is really part of what makes that person have the experience that they're having.
sentences.zh: 所有这一切，实际上都是造就这个人当前体验的重要部分。

sentences.en: And that sometimes with people who have very severe mental health problems, you know, unprocessed trauma is really quite important.
sentences.zh: 有时对于那些有非常严重心理健康问题的人来说，未处理的创伤真的很重要。

sentences.en: And it was quite late.
sentences.zh: 而且这个认识来得挺晚的。

sentences.en: I think it was only in the 80s, actually, that people started to recognize that a lot of these mental health problems that we work with, they're sitting on a sea of trauma.
sentences.zh: 我想直到80年代，人们才开始认识到，我们所处理的许多心理健康问题，其实都建立在创伤的海洋之上。

sentences.en: And if you don't deal with that trauma, then they're going to have relapse after relapse after relapse.
sentences.zh: 如果你不去处理这些创伤，那么他们就会经历一次又一次的复发。

sentences.en: So, thinking psychologically as a psychologist, that's what you're bringing to your ward round.
sentences.zh: 因此，作为一个心理学家进行心理学思考，这就是你带进查房的东西。

sentences.en: You're there to think as a psychologist, you know, the psychiatrist is thinking in terms of drugs or whatever.
sentences.zh: 你在那里是为了以心理学家的身份思考，你知道的，精神科医生是从药物或其他角度去思考的。

sentences.en: And some of the good ones will also think in terms of psychology, of course.
sentences.zh: 当然，其中一些优秀的医生也会从心理学的角度思考。

sentences.en: But you're there to really talk about, do we know about this?
sentences.zh: 但你的存在是为了真正探讨：我们了解这些吗？

sentences.en: Do we know anything about their background?
sentences.zh: 我们对他们的背景有所了解吗？

sentences.en: Do we know what their triggers are?
sentences.zh: 我们知道他们的触发因素是什么吗？

sentences.en: Do we know how they deal with their triggers?
sentences.zh: 我们知道他们是如何应对这些触发因素的吗？

sentences.en: Do we know how we can help them cope with the triggers?
sentences.zh: 我们知道如何帮助他们应对这些触发因素吗？

sentences.en: Do we know how we can help them, if they're hearing voices, hostile voices, have we been able to teach them ways in which they can learn to work with those voices?
sentences.zh: 如果他们听到声音、听到带有敌意的声音，我们是否能够教给他们一些方法，让他们学会如何与这些声音相处？

sentences.en: And so on and so on.
sentences.zh: 诸如此类，不一而足。

sentences.en: So, you're bringing your psychological knowledge into the ward round.
sentences.zh: 所以，你把你的心理学知识带进了查房中。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: And I guess just trying to really help bring forward that idea of a formulation, actually.
sentences.zh: 我想，这也正是在努力推动形成“案例构念”（formulation）的概念。

sentences.en: You know, and I think that can be so helpful.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我认为这真的非常有用。

sentences.en: And I'll often think about longitudinal formulation or just, yeah, like what has been, if we're weaving in compassion,
sentences.zh: 我经常会考虑纵向构念，或者，如果我们将同情心编织进去，

sentences.en: what has been their experience of how they've been spoken to and how they might then have internalised how they should speak to themselves and how it's okay to treat other people.
sentences.zh: 他们过去被对待的方式有着怎样的体验，这又会如何内化成他们对自己说话的方式，以及他们认为应该如何善待他人。

sentences.en: Like, so interesting.
sentences.zh: 真的太有趣了。

sentences.en: I mean, the classic position, I think, is it's not what's wrong with you, it's what's happened to you.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，经典的立场我想是：重要的不是你怎么了，而是你经历了什么。

sentences.en: So psychology is what's happened to you, as opposed to what's wrong with you.
sentences.zh: 所以心理学关注的是你经历了什么，而不是你出了什么毛病。

sentences.en: Yeah, and there's a very big shift.
sentences.zh: 是的，这是一个非常大的转变。

sentences.en: And I think even when we look at individual families, you know, the same parents, the same house, even,
sentences.zh: 而且我认为，甚至当我们审视单个家庭时，同样的父母，甚至同样的房子，

sentences.en: that children have been born into can still lead to very different outcomes for that child.
sentences.zh: 出生的孩子也可能走向截然不同的结局。

sentences.en: Because, of course, time has changed those parents.
sentences.zh: 因为，时间改变了父母。

sentences.en: Time has changed the world in between those siblings being born.
sentences.zh: 在这些兄弟姐妹出生的间隙，时间也改变了世界。

sentences.en: You know, I think I was a very different parent for my first baby than I was for my second, just because of life circumstances and, I don't know,
sentences.zh: 你知道，我想我对第一个孩子的育儿方式和对第二个孩子的育儿方式非常不同，仅仅是因为生活环境的不同，还有，我不知道，

sentences.en: the way that I felt about the world.
sentences.zh: 我对这个世界的感受方式。

sentences.en: And my dad was very well, very healthy when I was pregnant with my eldeSt.
sentences.zh: 我怀着大宝时，我爸爸身体非常好、非常健康。

sentences.en: But by the time my second came along, he'd been diagnosed with cancer.
sentences.zh: 但到老二出生时，他已经被诊断出患有癌症。

sentences.en: So my kind of hope and availability was very different for both of those babies.
sentences.zh: 因此，我对这两个孩子的期许和陪伴状态是截然不同的。

sentences.en: And so I think sometimes just thinking about context, yeah, and what has been that child's experience, but what has been their family's experience can be really helpful as well.
sentences.zh: 所以我觉得，有时候思考一下语境，以及那个孩子的经历是什么，他们的家庭经历是什么，真的会很有帮助。

sentences.en: Very much so.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: Very much so.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: And also, children are themselves.
sentences.zh: 而且，孩子们本身就是独立的个体。

sentences.en: Anna Freud would say babies are themselves, right?
sentences.zh: 安娜·弗洛伊德会说婴儿就是他们自己，对吧？

sentences.en: They're not all clones.
sentences.zh: 他们可不是什么克隆体。

sentences.en: They're not exact clones.
sentences.zh: 他们不是精准的复制品。

sentences.en: They all have different personalities, different needs.
sentences.zh: 他们都有着不同的性格、不同的需求。

sentences.en: They relate in different ways.
sentences.zh: 他们以不同的方式与人建立联系。

sentences.en: You know, very active children relate to passive mothers, very different to shy children, for example.
sentences.zh: 你看，非常活跃的孩子和被动的母亲交往的方式，就和害羞的孩子有很大不同。

sentences.en: So you're absolutely right about that.
sentences.zh: 所以你说的完全正确。

sentences.en: I mean, it's very important.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这非常重要。

sentences.en: The individual difference is extremely important in clinical psychology.
sentences.zh: 个体差异在临床心理学中极其重要。

sentences.en: It really is.
sentences.zh: 真的非常重要。

sentences.en: It really is.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: And I want to thank you for something you said earlier as well, which was really important, kind of giving permission for, you know,
sentences.zh: 我也想感谢你刚才说的另一件非常重要的事情，那就是给予人们某种许可，

sentences.en: scratching those itches that you're interested in.
sentences.zh: 去探索那些你感兴趣的“痒点”。

sentences.en: That's really important, even if you've been told, no, this will be better for you.
sentences.zh: 这真的很重要，哪怕有人对你说“不，这对你更好”，

sentences.en: Like, you should do this.
sentences.zh: 或者“你应该做这个”。

sentences.en: But, you know, giving yourself permission to come back to it.
sentences.zh: 但是，允许自己重新回过头去探索它。

sentences.en: But also role modelling that actually, even when we get to become clinical psychologists, we may well have failed things along the way.
sentences.zh: 同时这也是一种身教，实际上，即便我们成为了临床心理学家，我们在路上也可能会遭遇失败。

sentences.en: I certainly failed my first attempt at a probability module when I was at university.
sentences.zh: 我在大学时，概率论模块第一次考试绝对是挂了的。

sentences.en: You know, you failed your kind of first attempt at the kind of bio-physiology, I think you said.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，你刚才也提到，你对生物生理学的第一尝试好像也失败了。

sentences.en: Like, it doesn't mean that you should give up, does it?
sentences.zh: 这并不意味着你应该放弃，对吧？

sentences.en: No, no, no.
sentences.zh: 不，不，不。

sentences.en: It's okay to have another go.
sentences.zh: 再试一次是完全可以的。

sentences.en: Yeah, I got really good at it because I had a whole year just to do it.
sentences.zh: 对，我后来把那门课学得特别好，因为我有一整年的时间专门攻克它。

sentences.en: Okay, so there might almost be that post-traumatic growth about what happens when we give ourselves more time and have another go in a more focused way.
sentences.zh: 好，所以这可能有点类似于创伤后成长，也就是当我们给自己更多时间、以更专注的方式再试一次时会发生的事情。

sentences.en: I think that's a really crucial point, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 我认为这是一个至关重要的观点，对吧？

sentences.en: The secret of success is the ability to fail.
sentences.zh: 成功的秘诀在于拥有失败的能力。

sentences.en: We often used to say that to the clients, you know, but no, you've got to help me succeed.
sentences.zh: 我们以前经常对来访者这样说，但他们会说：“不，你得帮我成功。”

sentences.en: No, I'm going to help you fail because if you can fail, you'll keep going when you fail and you'll get better.
sentences.zh: “不，我是要帮你们面对失败，因为如果你能承受失败，当失败来临时你就会坚持下去，然后你就会变得更好。”

sentences.en: So that's a very important point you make, Marianne.
sentences.zh: 所以，玛丽安，你提出的这一点非常重要。

sentences.en: Yeah, it really is.
sentences.zh: 是的，确实如此。

sentences.en: And it, you know, absolutely.
sentences.zh: 而且，完全是这样。

sentences.en: And I think especially when we're told, you know, what actually first, I only decided to become a clinical psychologist in the very end weeks of my undergraduate degree.
sentences.zh: 我想尤其是当我们听到……其实我直到本科生涯的最后几周，才决定要成为一名临床心理学家。

sentences.en: And I don't know what it says about me that this was what piqued my interest, was that I was told from a clinical psychologist standing on a stage,
sentences.zh: 我不知道这说明了我什么，但最激起我兴趣的是，我听到一位站在台上的临床心理学家说：

sentences.en: which is a really hard career, I wouldn't recommend you to try.
sentences.zh: “这是一条非常艰难的职业道路，我不建议你们尝试。”

sentences.en: It's not a great narrative, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 这可不是什么美妙的说法，对吧？

sentences.en: It is true.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: And actually, I'm so glad I did try because I genuinely love what I do.
sentences.zh: 说实话，我很高兴我尝试了，因为我真心热爱我的工作。

sentences.en: I love the variety of my work and I just don't, I don't get that sense in the same way of, oh, I've got to do that thing or I've got to do that session.
sentences.zh: 我热爱我工作的多样性，我不会有一种感觉，比如“天哪，我非得去做那件事”或者“我非得去上那个会”。

sentences.en: Like I get, I get to do this.
sentences.zh: 而是“我能去做这个”。

sentences.en: I genuinely feel that's, that's how I feel about my work.
sentences.zh: 我真的由衷地对我的工作抱有这种感觉。

sentences.en: And I know not everyone feels like that about, about their jobs and their, their occupation.
sentences.zh: 我知道并不是每个人对他们的工作和职业都有这种感觉。

sentences.en: So I feel really fortunate that I do.
sentences.zh: 所以我感到非常幸运，我拥有这样的工作。

sentences.en: Yes, it's a point, it's a great point.
sentences.zh: 是的，说得对，这真是个极好的观点。

sentences.en: I mean, I mean, you know, the fact that you might not always enjoy it doesn't mean to say that you don't want to do it, right?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你可能并不总是享受它，但这并不意味着你不想去做它，对吧？

sentences.en: Because there's these different types of positive emotions, isn't there?
sentences.zh: 因为正向情绪有不同的类型，不是吗？

sentences.en: One of which is about the positive emotion we get from doing meaningful things.
sentences.zh: 其中之一就是我们从做有意义的事情中获得的积极情绪。

sentences.en: So like changing your baby's nappies and things that might not be so pleasant, but it's meaningful.
sentences.zh: 比如给婴儿换尿布之类的事情，可能不那么令人愉快，但它是意义重大的。

sentences.en: All right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: We do things not because they're pleasant, but because they're meaningful, they give us a sense of purpose and so on.
sentences.zh: 我们做事不是因为它们让人愉快，而是因为它们有意义，它们赋予我们使命感等等。

sentences.en: So that's a very important point you make that if we're just, you know, yes, it is a very hard career.
sentences.zh: 所以你提出了一个非常重要的观点：如果我们只是……是的，这确实是一条艰难的职业道路。

sentences.en: And I think sometimes it's a, when you're faced with all the tragedies of life day in, day out, it can get a bit tricky at times, but it's meaningful.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为，当你日复一日地面临生活中所有的悲剧时，有时事情会变得有点棘手，但它是充满意义的。

sentences.en: You wouldn't give it up, you know, you still want to do that.
sentences.zh: 你不会放弃它，你知道，你依然想做这份工作。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And with that in mind, like you've kind of alluded to what's happening in the world at the moment, it feels challenging as a mother.
sentences.zh: 带着这一点，就像你刚才提到的目前世界上正在发生的事情，作为一个母亲，这让人觉得充满挑战。

sentences.en: It feels challenging as just a human.
sentences.zh: 仅仅作为一个普通人，这也让人觉得充满挑战。

sentences.en: It feels challenging as a clinical psychologiSt.
sentences.zh: 作为一个临床心理学家，这也让人觉得充满挑战。

sentences.en: And, you know, with the rise of AI as well, it's just a difficult, it's just a difficult time.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，随着人工智能的崛起，这真是一个艰难的时期。

sentences.en: And maybe, you know, you have more years and more wisdom than me.
sentences.zh: 也许，你的年资和智慧比我更深厚，

sentences.en: Like, has it, has it always felt like we're living in the most difficult time right now or, or, or, or is this especially challenging?
sentences.zh: 就像，我们是否一直觉得我们正生活在最艰难的时期，还是说，这个时期尤其具有挑战性？

sentences.en: No, no, you're, you're, you're, no, it's not especially challenging.
sentences.zh: 不，不，不，这并不是尤其具有挑战性。

sentences.en: In CFT, life is full of suffering.
sentences.zh: 在同情心聚焦疗法中，生活本就充满了苦难。

sentences.en: Life is very challenging.
sentences.zh: 生活极具挑战性。

sentences.en: I mean, you know, it wasn't so long ago we had the plague and something like half of the population was killed off.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，不久前我们还经历过瘟疫，大约一半的人口都因此丧生。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So we've always been confronted with diseases and violence, wars and so on.
sentences.zh: 所以我们一直都在面对疾病、暴力、战争等等。

sentences.en: Poverty, obviously, a lot of humans have lived in intense poverty for many thousands of years.
sentences.zh: 贫困也是如此，许多人类在几千年的时间里一直生活在极度贫困之中。

sentences.en: And as you know, we've lived in terrorist states mostly because with the evolution of agriculture, we got the development of the aggressive male and the dominant of the elites.
sentences.zh: 如你所知，我们生活在恐怖国家中，这主要是因为随着农业的发展，出现了好斗的男性和精英阶层的统治。

sentences.en: So you look at the Assyrians, the Egyptians, the Romans, all of them, they were all terrorist states.
sentences.zh: 所以你看亚述人、埃及人、罗马人，所有这些，它们全都是恐怖国家。

sentences.en: They were just persecute 30% of the population in Rome were slaves, right?
sentences.zh: 它们只是在肆意迫害……罗马30%的人口都是奴隶，对吧？

sentences.en: If you look at the reign of Henry VIII, thousands of people were hung in London for crimes such as stealing a loaf of bread.
sentences.zh: 如果你回顾亨利八世的统治时期，成千上万的人在伦敦被绞死，罪名仅仅是偷了一条面包。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: We forget all this because we're living, we've gone through, we're going through periods where things are getting a lot better.
sentences.zh: 我们把这些全都忘了，因为我们生活在，我们已经经历过，我们正在经历这样一个时期：事情正在变得好得多。

sentences.en: And medicine does some miracle stuff now.
sentences.zh: 而且医学现在能创造一些奇迹般的成果。

sentences.en: You know, starvation is not common in Europe, at leaSt.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，至少在欧洲，饥饿已经不再普遍。

sentences.en: I mean, it's been used as a weapon of war, obviously, which is horrible.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，它显然被当作了一种战争武器，这太可怕了。

sentences.en: So because things have been really good, we look at these things.
sentences.zh: 所以，正因为情况一直以来都非常好，我们才会去看待这些事情。

sentences.en: Oh, my God, everything's getting worse.
sentences.zh: 天哪，一切都在变糟。

sentences.en: It's nothing like it was a few hundred years ago.
sentences.zh: 这跟几百年前的情况根本没法比。

sentences.en: So that's important to see that on the whole, humans are improving.
sentences.zh: 所以，认识到人类总体上是在进步，这一点很重要。

sentences.en: The key area that we have to improve is not our technologies and our medicines.
sentences.zh: 我们需要改进的关键领域并非我们的技术和医学。

sentences.en: And so we do need to improve that.
sentences.zh: 当然，这些我们确实需要改进。

sentences.en: It's our minds and how we choose our leaders.
sentences.zh: 而是我们的思想，以及我们如何选择领导人。

sentences.en: As it is at the moment, leadership is the most damaging of all human things, right?
sentences.zh: 就目前而言，领导力是所有人类事务中最具破坏性的，对吧？

sentences.en: The leaders that are getting to businesses of power, particularly these narcissistic and psychopathic.
sentences.zh: 那些爬上权力岗位的领导者，尤其是那些极度自恋和具有精神病态的人。

sentences.en: And we have to understand how do they get voted in?
sentences.zh: 我们必须搞懂，他们是怎么被投票选出来的？

sentences.en: How do they get supported?
sentences.zh: 他们是怎么获得支持的？

sentences.en: Because it's the leaders that are actually causing so many difficulties.
sentences.zh: 因为正是这些领导者实际上造成了如此之多的困境。

sentences.en: And it's also in like in the AI industries and the fossil industries, all of these individuals, if they lack a compassion focus, then they're careless and they will cause mayhem.
sentences.zh: 而且在人工智能行业和化石燃料行业等领域也是如此，所有这些人，如果他们缺乏同情心，那么他们就会粗心大意，并引发混乱。

sentences.en: So it's not so much the process of change, it's who's in control of that process of change, which is a real kind of worry, I think.
sentences.zh: 所以，重要的其实不是变革的过程，而是谁在掌控这个变革的过程，这真让人有点担心，我觉得。

sentences.en: And it is a bit of a worry.
sentences.zh: 这确实有点让人担心。

sentences.en: But I'm not pessimistic because I think there are sufficient numbers of people in the world who have a genuine compassion.
sentences.zh: 但我并不悲观，因为我认为世界上有足够多的人怀有真诚的同情心。

sentences.en: Most people want to be compassionate.
sentences.zh: 大多数人都希望充满同情心。

sentences.en: And if we can get the right leadership, then I think we can move the world to a more compassionate place.
sentences.zh: 如果我们能选出正确的领导层，那么我认为我们可以把世界带向一个更有同情心的地方。

sentences.en: And we could talk about that.
sentences.zh: 我们可以聊聊这个。

sentences.en: We're doing a lot of work on that.
sentences.zh: 我们在这方面做了很多工作。

sentences.en: But so the key thing is don't lose hope.
sentences.zh: 所以关键的一点是，不要失去希望。

sentences.en: Yes, things are tricky and all kinds of conflicts going on and so on and so on.
sentences.zh: 是的，事情确实很棘手，各种冲突不断发生，诸如此类。

sentences.en: But our movement on diseases is getting better.
sentences.zh: 但我们在战胜疾病方面的进展正在变得更好。

sentences.en: Where, you know, we just had COVID and we evolved this amazing vaccine that actually saved millions.
sentences.zh: 你看，我们刚刚经历了新冠疫情，我们研发出了这种惊人的疫苗，实际上挽救了数百万人的生命。

sentences.en: I mean, that would never have happened in any other part of history, but we're getting the technologies.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这在历史上的任何其他时期都是不可能发生的，但我们正在掌握这些技术。

sentences.en: And yes, the pharmaceutical companies were profiteering, didn't give the vaccines to the developing countries and so on.
sentences.zh: 是的，制药公司在大发横财，没有把疫苗分发给发展中国家，诸如此类。

sentences.en: But the key thing is that we can do it if we choose to do it.
sentences.zh: 但关键在于，只要我们选择去做，我们就能够做到。

sentences.en: And there are people now working in AI about how do you create a moral basis for AI.
sentences.zh: 而且现在有人工智能领域的从业者正在研究如何为人工智能建立道德基础。

sentences.en: And that's really important because AI, if we don't, then AI will be problematic.
sentences.zh: 这真的非常重要，因为如果不这样做，人工智能就会带来大麻烦。

sentences.en: So I think, you know, there are really good people in the world as well.
sentences.zh: 所以我觉得，世界上确实也有非常好的人。

sentences.en: And I always look to them rather than the not so good people.
sentences.zh: 我总是把目光投向他们，而不是那些不太好的人。

sentences.en: So, yes, I'm kind of hopeful in the long term.
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，从长远来看，我还是抱有希望的。

sentences.en: But yes, life is suffering and no doubt there will be more suffering ahead.
sentences.zh: 但是，是的，生命就是苦难，毫无疑问，前方还会有更多的苦难。

sentences.en: And that's a really helpful reminder.
sentences.zh: 这是一个非常受用的提醒。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你。

sentences.en: And I think that's one I'll keep drawing on for sure.
sentences.zh: 我想我以后肯定会经常汲取这一点。

sentences.en: Yeah,
sentences.zh: 对啊，

sentences.en: like it's I think when we're looking at kind of what we can achieve within our career and it's fair to say you've achieved a great deal and are still still striving to achieve more.
sentences.zh: 就像，我认为当我们审视我们在职业生涯中能取得什么成就时——可以公平地说，你已经取得了巨大的成就，并且仍在努力取得更多成就。

sentences.en: But when you're at the early part of a career, perhaps even still just considering becoming a psychologist, how do you not burn out when you see the challenges before you,
sentences.zh: 但当你处于职业生涯的早期，甚至可能只是在考虑成为一名心理学家时，当你看到摆在面前的种种挑战时，你该如何避免精疲力竭？

sentences.en: you know, with apparently mental health being worse than it ever has been, certainly in the UK?
sentences.zh: 你知道的，心理健康状况似乎比以往任何时候都要糟糕，在英国绝对是这样。

sentences.en: And the level of kind of dissatisfaction and poverty and and trauma.
sentences.zh: 还有那种种的不满、贫困以及创伤。

sentences.en: How do you how do you how do you feel enough just as a drop in that ocean?
sentences.zh: 你如何能够——仅仅作为沧海一粟——觉得这就够了？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Don't be narcissistic, basically.
sentences.zh: 基本上，别太自恋。

sentences.en: That's what I was a friend of mine who had talked about this a few years ago, because if you're doing that,
sentences.zh: 这就是几年前我和一个讨论过这件事的朋友所说的话，因为如果你那样做，

sentences.en: you're just assuming you've got or you should have more power than you don't.
sentences.zh: 你只是在假设你拥有、或者你本该拥有比实际更多的权力。

sentences.en: There's a wonderful story.
sentences.zh: 有一个很棒的故事。

sentences.en: It's a feminist story.
sentences.zh: 这是一个女权主义的故事。

sentences.en: It's just a lovely little story.
sentences.zh: 这是一个非常可爱的小故事。

sentences.en: So this guy and his girlfriend are walking along the beach and there's been a massive storm and all of these starfish are thrown up onto the beach.
sentences.zh: 有个男人和他的女朋友在海滩上散步，刚刚经历了一场大风暴，所有的海星都被冲到了沙滩上。

sentences.en: There's thousands and thousands of them.
sentences.zh: 有成千上万只。

sentences.en: And then she's walking along.
sentences.zh: 然后她一边走着，

sentences.en: She's picking one up and throwing it back.
sentences.zh: 一边捡起一只扔回海里。

sentences.en: And the guy says, so what are you doing that for?
sentences.zh: 男的就说，你这么做是为了什么？

sentences.en: I mean, there's thousands of them.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这里有成千上万只呢。

sentences.en: And she said, because it matters to the one I throw back.
sentences.zh: 她说，因为这对于我扔回海里的那一只来说意义重大。

sentences.en: So the point is, don't focus on the big picture.
sentences.zh: 所以重点是，不要只盯着宏大的全局。

sentences.en: All right.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: Because if you do that, you'll get overwhelmed.
sentences.zh: 因为如果你那样做，你会被压垮的。

sentences.en: That's just, you can't do that.
sentences.zh: 那根本行不通，你做不到。

sentences.en: What you can do is to focus on you, what you can do, what your values are, what your intentions are,
sentences.zh: 你能做的是专注于你自己，专注于你能做什么，你的价值观是什么，你的意图是什么，

sentences.en: how you will try to create a better world in the world that you can operate within.
sentences.zh: 在你能够施展影响力的世界里，你将如何努力创造一个更美好的世界。

sentences.en: So you bring that.
sentences.zh: 所以你要做到这一点。

sentences.en: But you're not, don't expect that you have got the power to produce a lot of changes because then you will get overwhelmed.
sentences.zh: 但你不要、不要指望自己有能力带来巨大的改变，因为那样你会被压垮的。

sentences.en: Now, the other side of that is that we also worry for our children.
sentences.zh: 另一方面，我们也会为我们的孩子感到担心。

sentences.en: And so what we then realize is that part of the anxiety is not for us.
sentences.zh: 所以我们随后意识到，这种焦虑其实有一部分不是为了我们自己。

sentences.en: It's for our children and our grandchildren.
sentences.zh: 是为了我们的孩子和孙辈。

sentences.en: And that's compassionate.
sentences.zh: 这充满着同情心。

sentences.en: How can I protect them from the potential horrors ahead?
sentences.zh: 我该如何保护他们免受未来潜在恐怖状况的伤害？

sentences.en: And that's a different issue of thinking about how we can do that.
sentences.zh: 这是一个关于我们如何做到这一点的不同维度的思考。

sentences.en: So it's an important point.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一个重要的观点。

sentences.en: Don't get overwhelmed by the problems because you're not going to be able to do that.
sentences.zh: 不要被这些问题压垮，因为你单凭一己之力无法解决所有问题。

sentences.en: But what you can do is to focus on what you can do and, you know,
sentences.zh: 但你能做的是专注于你能做的事，而且，

sentences.en: bring compassion to whatever you're doing and also thinking about what is your anxiety or probably your anxiety is mostly about your children and your grandchildren and your friends.
sentences.zh: 无论你在做什么都要带入同情心，同时思考你的焦虑是什么——可能你的焦虑主要还是关于你的孩子、孙辈和朋友。

sentences.en: And therefore, it's thinking about what how what would help me cope with the worries that I have about them.
sentences.zh: 因此，这是在思考，有什么方法能帮助我应对因他们而产生的担忧。

sentences.en: Yeah, that is such important advice.
sentences.zh: 是的，这真的是非常重要的建议。

sentences.en: And even thinking about people working in perhaps NHS services that have got long waiting lists is actually that starfish example is really powerful.
sentences.zh: 甚至想想那些在国民保健署（NHS）工作、面临漫长等待名单的人，那个海星的例子其实非常有力量。

sentences.en: So, yeah, there might be multiple years wait to get into this service, but actually I can do this assessment and do it really, really well.
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，可能需要等好几年才能进入这项服务，但实际上我可以做好这次评估，而且要把它做得非常非常出色。

sentences.en: Or the person that I finally picked up off that waiting list, that matters because this person matters.
sentences.zh: 或者我最终从那个等待名单上接诊的那个人，这很重要，因为这个人很重要。

sentences.en: And I almost can't can't be too consumed with with everything else that's waiting and all the people I don't feel like I can help right now.
sentences.zh: 我几乎不能、不能被其他所有还在等待的人以及那些我目前觉得无力帮助的人所吞噬。

sentences.en: Yes, I think that's that's really, really, really important to focus on what you can do, not what you can't.
sentences.zh: 是的，我认为这真的、真的、非常重要，要专注于你能做的事，而不是你做不到的事。

sentences.en: And the other thing is that it's very easy to get caught up in anger.
sentences.zh: 另一件事是，人们非常容易陷入愤怒之中。

sentences.en: I get very angry because I've seen how the underfunding of government after government, the callousness of government in relationship to health is just appalling.
sentences.zh: 我曾经非常愤怒，因为我看到了一届又一届政府对资金的克扣，看到政府在医疗问题上的冷酷无情，简直令人发指。

sentences.en: We're working with a group called Compassion in Politics and they're they're working with young politicians.
sentences.zh: 我们正在和一个叫作“政治中的同情心”（Compassion in Politics）的组织合作，他们在与年轻的政治家合作。

sentences.en: And the young, some of the young, on both sides of the house, actually,
sentences.zh: 而且年轻的政客中，议会两党的一些年轻人，实际上

sentences.en: are beginning to talk about we do need to have a more compassionate solutions to the problems that we're facing.
sentences.zh: 已经开始谈论我们需要为我们所面临的问题找到更多富有同情心的解决方案。

sentences.en: The older folks, my age folks, they're a pain in the ass, but the younger ones are really getting the message that we need a much more compassionate society.
sentences.zh: 那些老一代人，像我这个年纪的人，简直是个讨厌鬼，但年轻一代真的领会到了我们需要一个更具同情心的社会的精神内核。

sentences.en: It can't all be about checkbooks and accounts and money.
sentences.zh: 不能一切都只谈支票簿、账目和金钱。

sentences.en: And the health service is an example of extraordinary callousness at the level of politics, extraordinary callousness is shocking, really.
sentences.zh: 医疗服务就是政治层面极端冷酷的一个例子，那种极端的冷酷真的很令人震惊。

sentences.en: But there we are.
sentences.zh: 但事已至此。

sentences.en: People keep voting for them.
sentences.zh: 人们还是一直在投票给他们。

sentences.en: But you can't get too caught up in personal because then it just makes you very angry.
sentences.zh: 不过你不能太深陷于个人情绪中，因为那只会让你变得非常愤怒。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And I think when I was recruited to an 8A post, it was probably the anger and the indignance and the unfairness of it that actually drove me to be a really, really effective,
sentences.zh: 我想当我被录用担任一个8A级职位时，可能正是那种愤怒、愤慨和不公平感，驱动我成为了一个非常、非常有效率、

sentences.en: efficient clinician.
sentences.zh: 高效的临床医生。

sentences.en: So in my first week, I've been chatting to a member of staff and I said, oh, have you been finding finding it?
sentences.zh: 所以在我的第一周，我一直在和一位员工聊天，我说，哦，你觉得这里情况怎么样？

sentences.en: You know, the transition, it was kind of a remodeled service and the clinician had said, oh, I've been here about a year and I've seen one client so far.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，那个过渡期，那是一个重新改组的服务部门，那个临床医生说，哦，我来这儿大约一年了，目前为止只接待过一个来访者。

sentences.en: And I was like, well, sorry, one client and the clinician said, yeah, because, you know, you can't get the therapy rooMs.
sentences.zh: 我说，不好意思，只有一个来访者吗？那个临床医生说，对啊，因为你知道的，你根本借不到治疗室。

sentences.en: And I said, oh, but I I've been recruited to do a 50 percent face to face.
sentences.zh: 我说，哦，但我被招聘来是要承担百分之五十的面对面工作的。

sentences.en: And the client, the clinician had said, well, yeah, that won't happen because you can't get the rooMs.
sentences.zh: 那个临床医生就说，哦，那不可能发生，因为你根本借不到房间。

sentences.en: And I was like, well, I'll show you that.
sentences.zh: 当时我就想，好吧，我做给你看。

sentences.en: I'll show you.
sentences.zh: 我做给你看。

sentences.en: And so I was working four days at the time and I ended up being a peripatetic clinician.
sentences.zh: 所以当时我一周工作四天，最后我成了一个四处奔波的流动临床医生。

sentences.en: I was in that base only for half a half a day a week when I would just do admin.
sentences.zh: 我每周只有半天时间待在那个大本营里用来处理行政工作。

sentences.en: But I found myself clinic rooms all over the rest of the truSt.
sentences.zh: 但我自己在整个信托机构的其他地方找到了各种诊疗室。

sentences.en: I ultimately ended up seeing clients in a private room, in a library, in a health centre, in a community walk-in centre,
sentences.zh: 我最终在私人房间、图书馆、健康中心、社区步入式中心接待来访者，

sentences.en: in a mental health inpatient unit where they had a spare room.
sentences.zh: 甚至在一个有空房间的心理健康住院部里也接待过。

sentences.en: And I saw those clients and I got that waiting list down.
sentences.zh: 我接待了那些来访者，把等待名单缩短了。

sentences.en: So sometimes sometimes that can be helpful to activate our sense of drive.
sentences.zh: 所以有时候，这种经历确实有助于激活我们的驱动力。

sentences.en: But it did ultimately lead to me, I think, burning out of that of that role,
sentences.zh: 但它最终确实导致我，我觉得，对那个职位感到精疲力竭，

sentences.en: because if you're the only one that feels like you are doing those things and doing the work and seeing the things,
sentences.zh: 因为如果你是唯一一个觉得自己一直在做那些事、在拼命干活、在直面问题的人，

sentences.en: it's I find I find it hard to hard to continue that drive without just feeling a little bit sad, Paul.
sentences.zh: 保罗，我发现我很难在不感到一丝悲伤的情况下继续保持这种驱动力。

sentences.en: Yes, and I mean, the key issue, I think, there is why do other people feel disempowered to be able to do that?
sentences.zh: 是的，我的意思是，我认为这里的核心问题是，为什么其他人会觉得无能为力而无法做到这一点？

sentences.en: And we live in a society which subordinates people.
sentences.zh: 我们生活在一个使人们处于从属地位的社会里。

sentences.en: They don't question authority.
sentences.zh: 他们不敢质疑权威。

sentences.en: They don't fight back against, you know, because capitalist societies and all of these, it's some people call it patriarchy rule and that it teaches people to be subordinate.
sentences.zh: 他们不进行反抗，你知道的，因为资本主义社会以及所有这些体制——有些人称之为父权统治——它教导人们要服从。

sentences.en: Don't question, right?
sentences.zh: 不要质疑，对吧？

sentences.en: Well, somebody like you and the whole reason you've got a podcast, all that is immense energy to kind of try to make a difference.
sentences.zh: 然而像你这样的人，以及你做播客的所有原因，都需要付出巨大的能量去试图带来改变。

sentences.en: So, you know, it's a very special kind of energy that.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道的，这是一种非常特殊的能量。

sentences.en: So, but not everybody has that.
sentences.zh: 但是，并不是每个人都有这种能量。

sentences.en: And so it's about how do we inspire other people who might be more fragile, who might be more shy, who might be more anxious, but oh, no, we can't do that.
sentences.zh: 所以问题在于，我们如何去激励其他人——那些可能更脆弱、更害羞、更焦虑，觉得“哦不，我们做不到”的人。

sentences.en: How do we inspire them to be able to take the risks and have a go?
sentences.zh: 我们如何激励他们去承担风险并尝试一下？

sentences.en: I think it's really important.
sentences.zh: 我认为这真的非常重要。

sentences.en: I mean, yeah, I mean, when I was in the, we had to dictate when I was in the NHS, I don't know, about 20 years ago, we all had to cut our budgets.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，是的，当我在国民保健署工作时，大概20年前吧，我们都必须削减预算。

sentences.en: And all these managers came around and said, well, look, you know, you've got a part of the research and part of the clinical department.
sentences.zh: 所有这些经理走过来对我们说，看吧，你们这里有一部分是研究部门，一部分是临床部门。

sentences.en: So we need to cut the budget.
sentences.zh: 所以我们需要削减预算。

sentences.en: So we're going to take your secretary away.
sentences.zh: 因此我们要把你们的秘书调走。

sentences.en: I said, what are you talking about?
sentences.zh: 我说，你在说什么呢？

sentences.en: And they said, well, we just don't have any, you know, we've got to cut the thing.
sentences.zh: 他们说，嗯，我们就是没有，你知道的，我们必须削减开支。

sentences.en: I said, are you serious?
sentences.zh: 我说，你是认真的吗？

sentences.en: Are you going to take my secretary away so you'll pay me 40 pounds an hour to type a letter twice as slowly as my secretary could do it for five or whatever?
sentences.zh: 你要撤走我的秘书，然后付给我每小时40英镑去打字，速度比我的秘书用5英镑或其他费用能做到的慢上一倍？

sentences.en: I mean, it's ludicrous.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这太荒谬了。

sentences.en: They're just mad.
sentences.zh: 他们简直疯了。

sentences.en: All this payment by results.
sentences.zh: 搞什么按绩效付费。

sentences.en: We used to have, we used to run groups, you know, these, we used to run community groups and we'd bring in a group and we'd do some work with them for about 10 weeks,
sentences.zh: 我们以前常办小组活动，你知道的，这些社区小组活动，我们会把大家召集起来，跟他们一起工作大约10周，

sentences.en: particularly agoraphobics.
sentences.zh: 特别是针对广场恐惧症患者。

sentences.en: And then we'd have another 10 come in and the ones that had been treated would partner up with the other ones.
sentences.zh: 然后我们会迎来另外10个人，而那些已经接受过治疗的人会和新来的人结成搭档。

sentences.en: And so we developed this fantastic community of people and I'd keep an eye on them.
sentences.zh: 于是我们建立了一个非常棒的病友社群，我会一直关注着他们。

sentences.en: And if anybody was needed a little bit more help, we would see that.
sentences.zh: 如果有人需要更多的帮助，我们就会发现并提供援助。

sentences.en: And so then the payment by results came in.
sentences.zh: 然后“按绩效付费”的制度就出台了。

sentences.en: So they said, I can't do that.
sentences.zh: 他们说，我不能这么做了。

sentences.en: What do you mean I can't do that?
sentences.zh: 什么叫我不能这么做了？

sentences.en: Well, it's not an effective therapy.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这不是一种高效的疗法。

sentences.en: What do you mean it's not an effective?
sentences.zh: 什么叫这不是高效的疗法？

sentences.en: We're keeping people out of hospital, right?
sentences.zh: 我们在帮人们避免住院，对吧？

sentences.en: We're keeping people well.
sentences.zh: 我们在帮人们保持健康。

sentences.en: We're developing communities that is mutually supportive.
sentences.zh: 我们在建立相互支持的社区。

sentences.en: Yeah, but it's not in the nice guidelines, is it?
sentences.zh: 对，但这不是好指南里规定的，对吧？

sentences.en: What are you talking about?
sentences.zh: 你在说什么呢？

sentences.en: No, I've got to do that.
sentences.zh: 不，我必须得这么做。

sentences.en: You've got to do recognized psychological therapies.
sentences.zh: 你必须进行公认的心理疗法。

sentences.en: Just madness.
sentences.zh: 简直疯了。

sentences.en: So used to get so annoyed talking to them about actually people who are supported in their communities, right?
sentences.zh: 以前跟他们聊起真正支持社区里人们的人时，总是觉得很恼火，对吧？

sentences.en: And people feel valued and people paying attention to them and so on.
sentences.zh: 人们感到被重视，人们关注他们，诸如此类。

sentences.en: And Julian Abel has done some fantastic – he's got a wonderful book called The Compassion Project, which he was a physician doing at the end of life.
sentences.zh: 朱利安·阿贝尔做了一些非常棒的——他有一本精彩的书叫《同情项目》，那是他在临终关怀时作为一名医生写的。

sentences.en: And he's done some wonderful work about how you create compassionate communities that break into loneliness and have people talking together and de-shame and so on and so on.
sentences.zh: 他做了一些非常棒的工作，关于如何建立富有同情心的社区，打破孤独感，让人们聚在一起，消除羞耻感，诸如此类。

sentences.en: But, yeah, just – I mean, the NHS is nuts, basically.
sentences.zh: 但是，是的，就是——我的意思是，国民保健署简直就是疯了，基本上。

sentences.en: Absolutely nuts.
sentences.zh: 简直疯了。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: They're wonderful people that are, you know, fantastic skills.
sentences.zh: 他们都是很好的人，你知道的，技能非常棒。

sentences.en: The management and the funding of it is just nuts.
sentences.zh: 它的管理和资金简直是一团糟。

sentences.en: They really are.
sentences.zh: 它们确实如此。

sentences.en: I feel very privileged to have met the people I've met along my journey and, you know, either to keep them physically in my life or in my phone at the end of the phone.
sentences.zh: 我感到非常荣幸，在我的人生旅程中遇到了那些人，你知道的，要么让他们在现实生活中留在我的生活中，要么在电话那头。

sentences.en: But also it's what we learn about people that just stays with us, I think, during our journey in psychology.
sentences.zh: 但同样重要的是，我们对人们的了解会一直伴随着我们，我想，在我们心理学的人生旅程中。

sentences.en: It's such, such a privilege that I get to meet these people, that we get to have an impact on each other.
sentences.zh: 这真的是，真的是一种特权，我能遇到这些人，我们能够对彼此产生影响。

sentences.en: And then I get to carry their wisdom with me as I will carry yours with me in going forwards.
sentences.zh: 然后我带着他们的智慧前行，就像我未来也会带着你们的智慧一样。

sentences.en: Like, it's – we're really lucky.
sentences.zh: 就像是——我们真的很幸运。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: But the key point you're making is don't get caught up in all that.
sentences.zh: 但你提出的关键点是，不要陷入所有那些事情中。

sentences.en: Do what you can.
sentences.zh: 做你能做的事。

sentences.en: Of course, you do what you can.
sentences.zh: 当然，你做力所能及的事。

sentences.en: But if you get too caught up in it, then you will get burnt out because it is – it does make you very angry, quite understandably on behalf of the thing.
sentences.zh: 但如果你陷得太深，你就会筋疲力尽，因为这确实——这确实会让你非常生气，代表这件事生气也是完全可以理解的。

sentences.en: But that anger in the end is a bit of a poison and it will – you know, it's bad.
sentences.zh: 但这种愤怒到最后有点像毒药，它会——你知道的，这不好。

sentences.en: So it's recognising, look, I'll do what I can do and I'll do my best and that's it.
sentences.zh: 所以这是要认识到，听着，我会做我能做的事，我会尽力而为，就这样。

sentences.en: I can't do nothing more than that.
sentences.zh: 我做不到更多了。

sentences.en: And being able to come to terms with don't – oh, I should be able – this should happen, that should happen, that should happen.
sentences.zh: 并且能够接受不要——哦，我应该能够——这应该发生，那应该发生，那应该发生。

sentences.en: If you get into all of that, then it just winds you up.
sentences.zh: 如果你卷入所有这些，那么它只会让你心烦意乱。

sentences.en: So I always remember when I was young, I only disqualified and I was working in an acute unit because I've always worked in sort of the heavy end of the thing, as it were.
sentences.zh: 所以我总是记得我年轻的时候，我刚获得资格，我在一个急性病房工作，因为我一直从事比较繁重的那类工作，可以说是这样。

sentences.en: And so I was beginning to see a lot of clients with quite severe abuse and goodness knows what.
sentences.zh: 所以开始看到很多遭受严重虐待和天知道什么经历的客户。

sentences.en: So I went to my supervisor, who was a lovely lady.
sentences.zh: 所以我去找我的主管，她是一位可爱的女士。

sentences.en: She was psychodynamic.
sentences.zh: 她是心理动力学派的。

sentences.en: She passed away some years ago now.
sentences.zh: 她几年前已经去世了。

sentences.en: And in those days, you used to be able to smoke and she used to love smoking these French cigarettes.
sentences.zh: 在那个年代，你还可以抽烟，她很喜欢抽这种法国香烟。

sentences.en: The room was always full of smoke.
sentences.zh: 房间里总是烟雾缭绕。

sentences.en: And so I went to her and I said, Kitty, because that was her name, I said, look, I've got all these clients coming through now that I'm qualified.
sentences.zh: 所以我去找她，我说，基蒂，因为那是她的名字，我说，听着，自我获得资格以来，所有这些客户都来到我这里。

sentences.en: I'm being sent these referrals and they're really complicated and I don't know what I'm doing half the time.
sentences.zh: 我被转诊了这些案例，它们真的很复杂，我有一半时间都不知道自己在做什么。

sentences.en: Surely they can see somebody else.
sentences.zh: 他们肯定可以去看别人。

sentences.en: And she said, well, who?
sentences.zh: 她说，嗯，谁？

sentences.en: I said, well, I don't know.
sentences.zh: 我说，嗯，我不知道。

sentences.en: There must be somebody.
sentences.zh: 肯定有别人吧。

sentences.en: She said, no, no, there's only me and you.
sentences.zh: 她说，不，不，只有我和你。

sentences.en: We're the only psychologists in the service and my list are full.
sentences.zh: 我们是服务中仅有的心理学家，我的名单已经满了。

sentences.en: I said, oh, no, what am I going to do?
sentences.zh: 我说，哦，不，我该怎么办？

sentences.en: She said, so there must be somebody else.
sentences.zh: 她说，所以肯定有别人。

sentences.en: And he said, well, she said, well, she said, I suppose we'd all be much better off if Freud was still here.
sentences.zh: 他说，好吧，她说，好吧，她说，我想如果弗洛伊德还在的话，我们都会好过得多。

sentences.en: But unfortunately, he's dead.
sentences.zh: 但不幸的是，他去世了。

sentences.en: So we're going to have to manage without him.
sentences.zh: 所以我们得没有他也能应付。

sentences.en: And she said, look, the only thing you can do, you can be the best six month qualified psychologist you can be.
sentences.zh: 她说，听着，你唯一能做的，就是做一个资格六个月的、力所能及的最好的心理学家。

sentences.en: That's all you can be.
sentences.zh: 你只能做到这样。

sentences.en: You cannot be any more than that.
sentences.zh: 你不可能做到更多了。

sentences.en: You cannot give any more than that.
sentences.zh: 你不可能付出更多了。

sentences.en: In 20 years, you'll probably know a bit more than you do today.
sentences.zh: 20年后，你可能会比今天懂得稍微多一点。

sentences.en: But right now, you don't know 20 years.
sentences.zh: 但现在，你还不知道20年后的事。

sentences.en: You don't have 20 years experience.
sentences.zh: 你没有20年的经验。

sentences.en: And that's try to be the best you can in this moment.
sentences.zh: 所以要在此时此地努力做到最好的自己。

sentences.en: That's it.
sentences.zh: 就这样。

sentences.en: There's nothing else.
sentences.zh: 没有别的了。

sentences.en: OK, don't get caught up with anything else or the shoulds and oughts and blah, blah, blah, blah.
sentences.zh: 好的，不要被其他任何事情或各种“应该”和“本该”以及种种杂音所纠缠。

sentences.en: Just be what you can be.
sentences.zh: 做好你能做成的那个自己。

sentences.en: That's it.
sentences.zh: 就这样。

sentences.en: And, you know, if the world around you is burning, well, there's nothing you can do about that.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，如果周围的世界在燃烧，嗯，你也无可奈何。

sentences.en: And so it was really good.
sentences.zh: 所以这真的很好。

sentences.en: She was lovely to me and really helped me on my way and helped me to just ground myself in the doable and appreciate what I can do.
sentences.zh: 她对我很亲切，在我前行的路上给了我很多帮助，帮我把脚踏实地放在可行的事情上，并感激我能做到的事。

sentences.en: Rather than always thinking, well, I can't do and if only.
sentences.zh: 而不是总是想着，嗯，我做不到，如果当时怎样就好了。

sentences.en: Because, you know, when you're a young therapist, you have all these thoughts, you know, well, maybe if Beck was in the room or Freud was in the room or whoever,
sentences.zh: 因为，你知道，当你是一个年轻的治疗师时，你脑子里会有各种各样的想法，你知道，嗯，也许如果贝克在房间里，或者弗洛伊德在房间里，或者不管是谁，

sentences.en: maybe they'd see my incompetence and they'd wonder, how the hell did I get to be a clinical psych?
sentences.zh: 也许他们会看出我的无能，然后纳闷，我到底是怎么当上临床心理学家的？

sentences.en: All of those thoughts are coming to your head when you're new to the profession.
sentences.zh: 当你刚进入这个行业时，所有这些想法都会涌入你的脑海。

sentences.en: I don't know what the hell I'm doing half the time.
sentences.zh: 我有一半时间都不知道自己在干什么。

sentences.en: That's all natural.
sentences.zh: 这都很自然。

sentences.en: It's OK.
sentences.zh: 没关系的。

sentences.en: Don't worry about it.
sentences.zh: 别担心。

sentences.en: Just come bring yourself back to the moment.
sentences.zh: 把自己带回到当下。

sentences.en: OK, so maybe in 20 years, 30 years, I'll be better than I am now.
sentences.zh: 好吧，也许在20年、30年后，我会比现在更好。
